rule.title: Stop Windows Service Via Net.EXE
rule.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: Se ejecutó net.exe o net1.exe con el argumento "stop" para detener un servicio de Windows. Por sí sola es actividad administrativa común; el contexto define si es maliciosa.
es.what_it_detects: Creación de procesos donde Image termina en \net.exe o \net1.exe (u OriginalFileName es net.exe/net1.exe) y CommandLine contiene " stop ", es decir, "net stop <servicio>".
es.why_it_matters: Los atacantes detienen servicios (ATT&CK T1489, Service Stop) antes de cifrar datos o para desactivar defensas: antivirus, respaldos, VSS o bases de datos que bloquean archivos. El ransomware suele detener muchos servicios en lote.
triage_steps: Identifique en CommandLine qué servicio se detuvo; priorice seguridad (WinDefend, EDR), respaldos (VSS, Veeam), bases de datos (MSSQL*) y servicios de registro de eventos.
Revise ParentImage y la línea de comandos del padre: cmd.exe o powershell.exe desde un script desconocido, Office o un binario en %TEMP% es sospechoso.
Valide el usuario: ¿es una cuenta administrativa o de servicio esperada para ese host y horario?
Busque en el mismo host, +/- 15 minutos, otras ejecuciones de net stop, sc stop, taskkill, vssadmin delete shadows o bcdedit; varias seguidas indican preparación de ransomware.
Correlacione con ventanas de mantenimiento, despliegues de software o tickets de cambio para ese host.
Revise alertas previas del mismo host y usuario, inicios de sesión remotos (PsExec, WMI) y conexiones de red cercanas.
Confirme con los eventos 7036/7040 del Service Control Manager si el servicio quedó detenido o deshabilitado.
false_positives: Administradores que detienen servicios manualmente para mantenimiento o solución de problemas.
Instaladores, actualizadores y scripts de despliegue (SCCM, GPO) que detienen servicios antes de actualizar binarios.
Software de respaldo que detiene bases de datos o servicios durante la ventana de copia.
Scripts de monitoreo o automatización que reinician servicios con net stop / net start.
response_steps: Verifique con el dueño del sistema o el equipo de cambios si la detención estaba planificada.
Si no está justificada y afecta servicios de seguridad o respaldo, aísle el endpoint desde el EDR y preserve evidencia (árbol de procesos, script origen).
Reinicie los servicios detenidos y confirme su configuración de inicio; revise si fueron deshabilitados.
Restablezca credenciales de la cuenta usada si hay indicios de compromiso y busque la misma actividad en otros hosts.
Documente exclusiones para procesos padre y servicios legítimos recurrentes, para reducir ruido.
es.severity_rationale: Nivel bajo porque detener servicios es frecuente y legítimo; la alerta solo escala al combinarse con servicios críticos, padres inusuales o actividad de ransomware asociada.

en.summary: net.exe or net1.exe was run with the "stop" argument to stop a Windows service. On its own this is common admin activity; context decides whether it is malicious.
en.what_it_detects: Process creation where Image ends with \net.exe or \net1.exe (or OriginalFileName is net.exe/net1.exe) and CommandLine contains " stop ", i.e. "net stop <service>".
en.why_it_matters: Attackers stop services (ATT&CK T1489, Service Stop) before encrypting data or to disable defenses: antivirus, backups, VSS or databases that lock files. Ransomware often stops many services in bulk.
triage_steps: Read the service name in CommandLine; prioritize security (WinDefend, EDR), backup (VSS, Veeam), database (MSSQL*) and event logging services.
Check ParentImage and its command line: cmd.exe or powershell.exe launched from an unknown script, Office, or a binary in %TEMP% is suspicious.
Validate the user: is it an expected admin or service account for this host and time?
On the same host within +/- 15 minutes, look for more net stop, sc stop, taskkill, vssadmin delete shadows or bcdedit; bursts suggest ransomware staging.
Correlate with maintenance windows, software deployments or change tickets for the host.
Review earlier alerts for the same host and user, remote logons (PsExec, WMI) and nearby network connections.
Confirm via Service Control Manager events 7036/7040 whether the service actually stopped or was disabled.
false_positives: Administrators stopping services manually for maintenance or troubleshooting.
Installers, updaters and deployment scripts (SCCM, GPO) stopping services before replacing binaries.
Backup software stopping databases or services during the backup window.
Monitoring or automation scripts restarting services with net stop / net start.
response_steps: Confirm with the system owner or change team whether the stop was planned.
If unjustified and security or backup services are affected, isolate the endpoint via EDR and preserve evidence (process tree, source script).
Restart stopped services and verify their startup type; check whether they were disabled.
Reset credentials of the account used if compromise is suspected and hunt for the same activity on other hosts.
Document exclusions for recurring legitimate parents and services to reduce noise.
en.severity_rationale: Low level because stopping services is frequent and legitimate; it only escalates when combined with critical services, unusual parents or related ransomware activity.

positive.description: net.exe launched from a batch script in a temp folder stopping the SQL Server service
net1.exe child spawned by net.exe stopping the Volume Shadow Copy service

negative.description: net.exe used to start a service, no ' stop ' in the command line
Service stopped with sc.exe instead of net.exe, so the image selection does not match
